subject: brutalistBlock
pitch:
Category: Architecture.
Subject: brutalist housing block.
Style: raw concrete brutalism.
reasoning:
I'm planning a brutalist housing block as a single static model built from boxes—roughly 60m long, 20m deep, and 24m tall across eight storeys, standing on the ground facing +Z. I'm designing it as a slab with a modular egg-crate facade of recessed balconies and deep concrete frames.

I'm adding stair/lift towers at the ends and center, a pilotis ground floor on chunky columns, plus a roof plant box, water tank, and parapet, with concrete tones varying across panels for a board-formed look. I'm defining colors for the concrete variations, dark recesses, glass with warm lit windows, and accent-colored balcony panels in the Unité d'Habitation style, then laying out the structure: a 48m length, 14m depth, seven to eight storeys at 3m each, a 4m pilotis base, bays spaced every 4m, and paired tapered columns at each bay line forming the lobby core.

Now I'm detailing the facade system: a dark recessed interior wall, protruding vertical fins at each bay, horizontal floor slabs, and individual cells containing glass panes, colored balcony parapets, and lit windows, repeated across front and back sides using a shared helper function with a side parameter, keeping the part count manageable. I'm finishing with solid gable end walls with slit windows and board-formed ribs, plus protruding stair towers at the ends and a central rear tower, before capping the building with a parapet roof.

Working out rooftop elements now -- barrel-vaulted plant room boxes, chimney and water tank cylinders, a pergola on columns, and a sloped ramp box -- while calculating exact vertical positions for the parapet, floor slabs, and ground-level pilotis so columns rise cleanly from y=0 and each floor's cell geometry sits correctly between slabs. I'm also working out the depth offsets for the facade wall and frame elements relative to the building's total depth.

For each facade bay I'm placing full-depth slabs, vertical fins, recessed glass panels, thin balcony panels, and small mullions, while deciding to randomly light a portion of the windows warm for a lived-in night glow effect using the glow material, keeping flat colors for the rest. I'm also considering adding a rooftop sunshade, an entrance canopy, and a stair tower with slit windows.

Writing helper and tower geometry...
